topic: Leftward movement as a test for matrix adjuncts
claim: An adjunct after an auxiliary “can be moved to the left of the auxiliary if it belongs in the matrix, but not if it belongs in the subordinate clause”, as in [12ia] ∗He deeply had offended her. Then: “The best test is to see whether the adjunct can be moved to the left of the auxiliary: if so, this is strong evidence that it belongs in the matrix.”
evidence_summary: Ch. 6, p. 575 cites this section (“As noted in Ch. 8, §20.2”) and gives [4iib] ?They contentedly would watch TV for hours, where contentedly has its “basic position” in the watch clause. Page 578 [11iib] is ?Chris expertly had repaired it, the frame of [12ia], and “it should not be assumed that such sentences will never be encountered”.
finding: Medium confidence. By the p. 783 test, Ch. 6’s ?-marked examples would put the manner adjunct in the matrix, against Ch. 6’s own analysis. The defence that the starred adverbs in [12] aren’t manner adverbs (deeply is a degree adverb, and Ch. 6, p. 579 restricts degree adverbs in central position) saves the stars but not the rule, which is stated for adjuncts in general.
inference: Does placement before the auxiliary show that an adjunct belongs in the matrix?

evidence.passage: §20.2, p. 783. “The best test is to see whether the adjunct can be moved to the left of the auxiliary: if so, this is strong evidence that it belongs in the matrix.”
evidence.example: Ch. 6, p. 575 [4iib] ?They contentedly would watch TV for hours. Page 578 [11iib] ?Chris expertly had repaired it.
evidence.establishes: Ch. 6 grades placement of a subordinate-clause manner adjunct before the auxiliary as marginal, not excluded.
